body:
The operator's own instance runs `NETWORK_SHARE_MODE=true`. `cps/ub.py:4925-4940`
branches the app.db journal mode on exactly that flag: true means WAL is never
requested and app.db uses "legacy sqlite3 transaction control with a rollback
journal; call sites requiring contained SAVEPOINTs acquire a local write
transaction."

`prepare_user_library_seed` (cps/user_library.py:90-143) is built directly on that
machinery. Its own docstring says so:

    Each chunk is its own app.db transaction. That bounds the BEGIN IMMEDIATE
    write-lock window introduced by the contained-savepoint policy (#1936).

So the seed's transaction behaviour is a function of NETWORK_SHARE_MODE, and the
chunking exists specifically to bound a lock the flag changes the semantics of.

**No My Library test sets NETWORK_SHARE_MODE.** Verified across all three files:

    grep -n 'NETWORK_SHARE_MODE\|journal_mode\|WAL' \
        tests/unit/test_1939_migration_ordering.py \
        tests/unit/test_my_library_backend_1939.py \
        tests/unit/test_my_library_leg6_regressions.py
    (no matches)

Every rig runs the opposite of production:

| rig | NETWORK_SHARE_MODE | journal |
|---|---|---|
| production (operator's instance) | **true** | rollback journal |
| tests/conftest.py:765 | false | WAL |
| docker-compose.local.yml | false | WAL |
| docker-compose.dev-live.yml | false | WAL |
| docker-compose.bindmount.yml | false | WAL |

This is a coverage finding, not a known defect. The seed HAS run once on the real
configuration — 222 rows committed cleanly on the operator's instance, OBSERVED —
so there is no evidence of breakage. What is missing is anything that would keep
it working: the passing run was accidental (it happened because an unrelated
authorisation put me on the real instance), it covers one library size and zero
concurrency, and nothing in CI would catch a regression.

The specific risk the chunking was written to bound, and which is unmeasured
without WAL: under a rollback journal a write transaction takes a RESERVED lock on
the whole database, so a concurrent app.db writer blocks for the chunk's duration
rather than proceeding as it would under WAL. `connect_args={'timeout': 30}`
(cps/ub.py:4920) is the only thing standing between that and SQLITE_BUSY. Under
WAL — the only mode ever tested — writers never block readers at all, so the test
suite cannot observe this class by construction.

Note this is the same shape as `a-green-suite-can-be-incapable-of-detecting-its-own-bug`:
the suite is green and would stay green through a real regression, because the
predicate it exercises is not the one production runs.

resolution.note: Closed as a coverage gap; no production defect was found. Added one feature-level rollback-journal discriminator in tests/unit/test_my_library_backend_1939.py. With NETWORK_SHARE_MODE=true it builds the real app.db engine, observes journal_mode=delete and busy_timeout=30000, holds the first two-row seed chunk after its INSERT, directly proves an independent app.db write receives database-is-locked, and then requires a competing writer to commit before the seed may issue chunk two. The test therefore pins the reason prepare_user_library_seed commits every chunk, not merely final row correctness. Deliberately replacing the full-chunk app_session.commit() with app_session.flush() produced 1 failed in 5.74s: the competing writer could not cross the first seed chunk boundary. Restoring HEAD produced 1 passed in 0.41s. No elapsed-time or exact wait-duration assertion was added: scheduler and filesystem timing would be noise; the deterministic execution-event gates pin lock existence and the release boundary without sleeps.

title: the My Library seed is never exercised in the transaction mode production actually runs
